questions.question: A tank can be filled by two taps A and B in 8 hours and 10 hours respectively. The whole tank can be emptied by the third tap in 12 hours. If all the taps are turned on at the same time, in how much time (in how many hours) will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tap A fill the tank in 8 hours

Tap B fill the tank in 10 hours

Tap C empty the tank in 12 hours

**Concept used:**

Time = Work/Efficiency

**Calculation:**

LCM of 8, 10, 12 = 120

Total capacity of tank = 120 units

Efficiency of Tap A = 120/8 = 15 units

Efficiency of Tap B = 120 /10 = 12 units

Efficiency of Tap C = 120/ 12 = 10 units

Effective of these three tanks together = (15 + 12 – 10) = 17 unit

Time taken to fill the tank when they all opened simultaneously = 120 /17 = 7.0588 ≈ 7 hours

**∴ The empty tank be completely filled in 7 hours**

questions.question: A train overtakes two persons, who are traveling in the same direction as the train moving at 2 km/h and 4 km/h and passes them in 9 and 10 seconds respectively. Find the length and speed of the train-

Speed of first train = 2 km/h

Speed of second train = 4 km/h

Time taken to overtake the second person = 10 sec

If train running in same direction = (x – y) km/h

Speed = Distance / Time

Km/h × 5/18 = m/sec

**Calculation:**

Let the length of train be L

 According to the question

Speed of first person is

⇒ 9 = L/(x – 2 × 5/18) .....(1)

Speed of second person is

⇒ 10 = L/(x – 4 × 5/18) .....(2)

Now, substituting the equation (1) and (2) we get,

⇒ 9/10 = (x – 4)/(x – 2)

⇒ 9x – 18 = 10x – 40

⇒ x = (40 – 18)

⇒ x = 22 km/h

Putting the value of x in equation (1)

⇒ 9 = L/(20 × 5/18)

⇒ 9 = L/(100/18) m

⇒ 9 = L/(50/9)

⇒ L = (50 × 9)/9

⇒ L = 50 m

**∴ The required value is 22 km/h and 50 m**

Boys receive = z = 8

questions.question:
A question and two statements are given below. Identify which statement(s) is/are necessary/sufficient to answer the question?

Question:

How many students play cricket in the class?

Statement:

I. There are 32 boys and 28 girls in the class.

II. Only boys play cricket.

options.text: Data either in I alone or II alone is sufficient
Data in II alone is sufficient

Data in I alone is sufficient

questions.solution:
**Given:- **

Question:- How many students play cricket in the class?

**Statement I:- There are 32 boys and 28 girls in the school:-** This statement tells us the number of boys and girls in the class, but it does not provide any information about how many boys play cricket. Therefore, by itself, Statement I is not sufficient to answer the question.

**Statement II:- Only boys play cricket:- **This statement tells us that only boys play cricket, but it does not tell us how many boys are there or how many of those boys play cricket. Therefore, by itself, Statement II is also not sufficient to answer the question.

Both Statements I and II together:- However, even with both statements together, we still do not know how many of the 32 boys actually play cricket. There could be fewer than 32 boys playing cricket, or all 32 boys could play cricket. We need additional information specifying how many of the boys actually play cricket to provide a precise answer.

**Hence, Data in both I and II together is not sufficient to answer the question.**

• **Temperature** refers to the** hotness or coldness** of a body. In specific terms, it is the way of determining the **kinetic energy** of particles within an **object.** Faster the movement of particles; more the temperature and vice versa.
 
• The** three** most common** temperature scales** are the **Fahrenheit, Celsius**, and **Kelvin scales**.

 **Details**
 
 

 **Fahrenheit**
 
 __
 
• On the Fahrenheit scale, the freezing point of water is at 32ºF and the boiling point is at 212ºF.
 
• The temperature difference of one degree Celsius is greater than a temperature difference of one degree Fahrenheit.
 
• One degree on the Celsius scale is 1.8 times larger than one degree on the Fahrenheit scale 180/100=9/5.
 
 
 
 

 **Celsius**
 
 
 
• The Celsius scale has a freezing point of water as 0ºC and the boiling point of water as 100ºC.
 
• The temperature difference of one degree Celsius is greater than a temperature difference of one degree Fahrenheit.
 
• One degree on the Celsius scale is 1.8 times larger than one degree on the Fahrenheit scale 180/100=9/5.
 
 
 
 

 **Kelvin**

questions.question: A man sold two cycles at a total profit of 20%. If he had bought them each for 3,500 and the first one sold them at a profit of 5%, then what is the profit (%) he should have from the second?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total profit = 20%

Cost price of each cycle = Rs. 3500

Profit% on first cycle = 5%

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

According to the question

Total CP = Rs. (3500 + 3500) = Rs. 7000

Total SP = Rs. (7000 × 120/100)

⇒ Rs. 8400

Now,

SP of first cycle = Rs. (3500 × 105/100)

⇒ Rs. 3675

SP of second cycle = Rs. (8400 – 3675)

⇒ Rs. 4725

Profit = Rs. (4725 – 3500)

⇒ Rs. 1225

Profit% = (1225/3500 × 100)

⇒ 35%

**∴ Required profit percentage on second cycle is 35%**
